commits.message:
Add review cache for uswds-code-review skill

Reviewing a PR repeatedly re-runs every gate even when the commit hasn't
changed since the last pass. This adds a cache (.review-cache/, unversioned)
keyed on PR number and head commit SHA, so `check` reports a hit and returns
the prior findings instead of re-reviewing. Entries are never deleted: a
merged PR is marked `status: "merged"` and keeps its findings markdown, since
that's the record you want when a regression surfaces later.

The original draft of this also included a digest/reporting layer
(review-digest.mjs) on top of the cache, which pushed the change well past
this repo's PR size norms and mixed two concerns that don't need to land
together — nothing in the cache imports the digest module. That layer is
split into a follow-up PR; this PR is the cache alone.

Fixed before landing, rather than as follow-up patches:
- `reportPath` was stored as a fake repo-relative string and only
  reconstructed into a real path via a `resolveReportPath` indirection that
  existed solely to `basename()` it back apart. Collapsed into one
  `reportFilePath(cacheDir, sha)` helper computed directly from `cacheDir`,
  which also fixes `check --cache-dir <dir>` printing a report path that
  didn't actually exist.
- A corrupted cache.json was caught and silently replaced with an empty
  cache object; the next `save` would then overwrite the corrupt file with
  a fresh one, discarding every prior cached review with no error at all.
  `loadCache` now throws, and `main()`'s existing top-level catch surfaces
  it. Added a regression test asserting the corrupt file survives a failed
  save untouched.
- `check`'s CACHED and MERGED output were inconsistent (only CACHED showed
  the summary and a MISSING-ON-DISK flag); `list` never printed the summary
  and showed raw ISO timestamps. Unified via shared `printField`/
  `printCachedReview` helpers and a date-only formatter.
- `--rec` was a working alias for `--recommendation` but undocumented in
  --help; `--force` hardcoded its exit code instead of using the
  CHECK_EXIT_CODES table.

Runtime is still large for one PR (~740 lines), but a working cache is one
atomic unit and doesn't decompose further without the digest split already
taken out. Suggested reading order: cache I/O -> PR lookup -> check/save/sync
-> CLI.

Added `npm run test:agents` so the spec (deliberately kept out of `gulp
test`, since this is skill tooling rather than shipped library code) is
runnable without memorizing the raw mocha invocation.

commits.message:
fix(misc#356): let OpDiv admins write system attributes on systems in their OpDivs (#574)

Closes CMS-Enterprise/ztmf-misc#356.

An OpDiv-scoped admin could not set FIPS or the other system attributes
on their own systems. `SaveFismaSystem` nilled `hva`, `fips`,
`system_type`, `cloud_system`, `cloud_service_model`, `cloud_vendor`,
`system_operator`, `goco_coco_gogo`, and `legacy` on POST and restored
the stored values on PUT for any caller without unscoped read, then
returned success. The frontend has let every write admin edit those
fields since ztmf-ui#459, so an HRSA admin saw an editable field whose
value never persisted (reported by HRSA on 2026-08-28).

The gate's stated purpose was partial-PUT protection for fields the form
could not edit. `Save` already provides that for everyone: an omitted or
null field leaves the stored value untouched. So this removes
`clearUnscopedOnlyFields` and `preserveUnscopedOnlyFields` and their
branch. The update path keeps `guardManageFismaSystem` for callers
without unscoped read, so an OPDIV_ADMIN still gets 403 on a system
outside their granted OpDivs and 404 on a missing one. OWNER and
HHS_ADMIN paths are unchanged, and read-only tiers are still rejected at
`IsAdmin()`.

`fismasystems_metadata_test.go` is deleted; its four tests only
exercised the removed helpers. Emberfall Test B is rewritten: the OpDiv
admin's create now asserts every attribute persisted, the update sends a
different value for each attribute and contact field and the GET asserts
they landed, and a new case pins the cross-OpDiv PUT 403. `cloud_system`
stays true in the update because `Save` rejects a service model or
vendor when it is No.

Gate: `make test-unit` green, `make test-integration` green, `make
test-e2e` 219/219 (218 on main), `make generate-openapi` no drift. No
frontend change is needed; ztmf-ui already sends these fields.
commits.author: cameron testerman

commits.message:
chore(#317): SHA-pin every workflow action, retire the snyk @master refs, and replace staticcheck-action (#571)

Stacked on #559: this branch sits on top of it, so the diff here
includes #559's two commits until it merges. Once it does I will rebase
onto main so only the commit below remains, and mark this ready for
review. Draft until then.

Finishes ztmf#317 on top of #559. That PR moved the remaining actions to
their Node.js 24 majors; this one converts every ref it left as a
floating tag to a commit SHA with a version comment, matching the format
#349 established in backend.yml, and closes out the rest of the ticket's
acceptance criteria. Also closes CMS-Enterprise/ztmf-misc#173.

The two snyk/actions refs in analysis.yml were still on @master. All
three snyk/actions uses now pin the v1.0.0 tag (9adf32b, 2025-10-03);
comparing that tag to master head shows no changes under setup/,
golang/, or docker/, so this is a provenance change only, and it retires
the stale "no tagged releases" comment. aquia-inc/emberfall moves from a
main commit to the v0.5.0 tag, whose action.yml is byte-identical to the
previous pin; the binary stays at 0.4.1 via the version input.
docker/setup-buildx-action goes to v4.3.0 for parity across backend.yml
and ops-image.yml. The two setup-go blocks in analysis.yml gain
cache-dependency-path: backend/go.sum, which #349 only did for
backend.yml, so the openapi and snyk test jobs stop missing the cache on
every run.

The lint go job no longer uses dominikh/staticcheck-action. The
composite pins actions/cache to a Node.js 20 build (upstream
dominikh/staticcheck-action#22 and #23, master unchanged since March
2026), which was the one deprecation warning left after every other
bump. The job now installs staticcheck with go install after a setup-go
on Go stable, mirroring the composite's install-go default, since
staticcheck's latest release requires a newer Go than the go.mod floor
and setup-go v6+ sets GOTOOLCHAIN=local. The action's problem matcher is
checked in under .github/matchers/staticcheck.json so PR annotations
behave as before. The same commands run clean locally against backend/
on Go 1.26.5 with staticcheck 2026.2.1.

Verification: a script resolved every pinned SHA back to its tag through
the GitHub API and confirmed each action's runtime is node24 (or
composite/docker); no @vN, @master, or @main refs remain under
.github/workflows. actionlint reports the same 16 pre-existing
shellcheck notes as main and nothing new. ops-image.yml and
nightly-impl-sync.yml have no pull_request trigger, so their pins are
verified by the resolver rather than a run. .github/dependabot.yml
already carries the github-actions group from #349 and is unchanged.

Closes #317

The red Check for Changes is the #568 migration-currency guard: this
branch inherits #559's base, which is five commits behind main and
predates 0058eventspagination.go. It clears with the rebase once #559
merges; as a draft this PR does not deploy to dev, so the guard's
crash-loop scenario cannot occur here.

commits.message:
Improve test coverage for the largest views (#717)

* test(users): restore UserTable coverage and add mutation-flow tests

The 585-line `UserTable` suite was deleted in #614; its `buildFismaSystemsMap` tests were obsolete (that helper is gone) but the fetch-plumbing coverage still applied. Reinstate the surviving tests aligned to the current code (OpDivs from context, per-user assignable endpoint drives the picker, global reads fetched once and reused), and add the mutation flows that were never covered: delete with confirm, cancel as a no-op, the self-delete guard, a failed delete that keeps the row, and restore.

Create/edit run through the DataGrid inline-edit lifecycle, which the minimal grid mock does not drive; noted for separate coverage.

Refs #623

* test(systems): cover EditSystemModal core save, error routing, and create

The extended-metadata tests covered the edit path's dirty-diff; add the core-write coverage that was missing. Edit sends the full core record so an unrelated change cannot drop a field; a 400 field map routes each reason inline and keeps the modal open; create is gated until the required fields are filled; and a completed create form POSTs the correct body and reports success. Notes the datacenter-environment select's label-is-category, value-is-environment split.

Refs #623

* test(systems): cover SystemDetailPage decommission and reactivate flows

The page's core save was already exercised, but the state-changing decommission (`DELETE` with a date/notes body) and reactivate (`PUT /reactivate`) flows were not. Add coverage driving the real edit-view path (reveal the form, confirm the dialog, assert the request) plus the cancel-is-a-no-op guard so a dismissed confirmation never writes.

Refs #623

* test(questionnaire): add coverage for the questionnaire modal

The 632-line modal had no test. Cover the load chain (latest data call -> questions -> existing scores -> options), answering a question and saving a new score on Next (`POST` with the selected option and data call), and close. A regression here fails to load or record answers.

Refs #623

feat(tests): Ref cleanup.

* test(users): raise UserTable coverage past 80%

Drive the create/edit save path (processRowUpdate), the toolbar (add row, view toggles), edit-mode save/cancel, the OpDiv grant and per-user backfill, and column rendering via an upgraded grid mock. 52% -> 80%.

Refs #623

* test(systems): raise EditSystemModal coverage past 80%

Cover the create happy-path and error routing, the decommission/reactivate section, extended-control type branches,  and organization-field edits. 50% -> 81%.

Refs #623

* test(systems): raise SystemDetailPage coverage past 80%

Add read-view rendering, decommissioned-by/reactivated-by name resolution, the single-system fetch fallback, and the save/decommission/reactivate error paths. 65% -> 81%.

Refs #623

* test(questionnaire): raise QuestionnareModal coverage past 80%

Add the edit-existing-score PUT, back navigation, and the options-load effect on top of the load/create/close coverage. 75% -> 88%.

Refs #623

* test: raise the four largest views to 80% coverage and quiet test noise

Extend the UserTable, EditSystemModal, SystemDetailPage, and QuestionnareModal suites to at least 80% statement/line coverage: the create/edit save paths, decommission/reactivate flows, error routing, validation gates, and the questionnaire load-and-save chain. Where the production path runs through the MUI grid's inline-edit lifecycle, the mock captures processRowUpdate so the save is driven directly.

Also clears the console noise these suites emitted: fixture selects no longer carry values without matching options (was flooding out-of-range warnings), and the mocked grid action item forwards refs and props so the Tooltip wrappers stop warning.

Refs #623

* test(views): tighten coverage assertions for four largest views

Replace request-only and vacuous assertions with outcome-based ones so the coverage number reflects real behavior:

- UserTable: assert grant happy-path (setUserOpDivs + Saved toast), split toggle tests to assert effects, add real isCellEditable wiring test
- SystemDetailPage: TZ-safe decommission dates, assert notify + state updater flips, assert both names in read/edit views
- EditSystemModal: assert specific error toast on failed reactivate
- QuestionnareModal: drop dead mock handlers, guard against junk POST

* chore(tests): increase test timeout for CI environments

commits.message:
Some whimsy ✨ (#718)

* feat(questionnaire): celebrate a completed questionnaire with confetti

Fire a confetti burst in the completion summary when every question is answered and confirmed. Gated on the existing complete flag so incomplete calls never trigger it, and suppressed for users who prefer reduced motion.

The burst renders on a viewport-anchored canvas portaled to the body so it paints above the modal and is unaffected by dialog transitions.

Add canvas-confetti; stub it globally in test setup (no canvas context under jsdom) with a shared asserting mock for the confetti suites.

Closes #488

* fix(questionnaire): skip the confetti overlay entirely under reduced motion

Return null instead of portaling an unused canvas into the body when the user prefers reduced motion.

* test(confetti): add assertions for canvas presence in confetti burst tests
